grading_method: Manual semantic comparison of every requested part, independently per answer. Reader support labels do not decide grade.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Factory deck is placed on the Factory territory. Encounter tokens are placed on designated territories. Structure bonus setup is not described; only that final coins include structure bonus tile coins (which vary). Who starts is not stated.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “Place encounter tokens on designated territories. Place the Factory card deck on the Factory territory.” Final Scoring: “Plus structure bonus tile coins (varies).”
grades.reason: Missing players+1 random Factory selection/unseen removal, 11 marked encounters, random face-up structure tile, lowest-mat starter.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: The character starts on the faction's home base and one worker on each adjacent territory. Power and popularity markers start at positions that vary by Faction mat. Starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards are received as indicated, but the summary does not specify their amounts or clearly identify which mat supplies each. Other map and mat starting pieces are not specified.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “Place the character on the faction's home base and one worker on each adjacent territory. Set combat power and popularity markers at starting positions (varies by Faction mat). Receive starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards as indicated.”
grades.reason: Incorrectly attributes popularity to Faction Mat; it is supplied by Player Mat. Mat setup and two land-adjoined worker specificity also incomplete.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, you may take one action, both, or neither, but must move your action token. You cannot repeat the same section as your previous turn, except Rusviet may repeat the same action section on consecutive turns. The summary says to perform the top-row action before the optional bottom-row action, but does not explicitly say whether taking the bottom action first is prohibited. Whether top-row gains can be spent on the bottom action is not stated. Bottom-row actions are described as paying their cost and gaining their benefit; exact costs are shown in the action descriptions, with Produce's cost variable.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “You may take one action, both, or neither, but you must move your token.” Turn step: “cannot repeat the same section as your previous turn.” Rusviet exception: “can repeat the same action section on consecutive turns.”
grades.reason: Missing full exposed red-cost payment, optional green benefit, using top gains below and explicit bottom-first prohibition.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: The summary says resources on a territory belong to whoever controls that territory, but does not explain who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker or who can use its structure. For action spending elsewhere, the summary only states that Trade resources are gained on territories you control with workers; it does not state the general locations from which resources may be spent.
grades.reader_evidence: Special Rules: “Resources on a territory belong to whoever controls that territory.” Trade: “Gain 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers.”
grades.reason: No ruling for enemy unit control, persistent owner structure abilities/Mill exception or remote resource spending.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: On a normal Move, up to two units may each move one territory; the summary does not say a unit can move twice. Mechs can carry workers, and workers carry resources. Whether a worker transported by a mech may then move separately is not stated.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Move up to 2 units (character, worker, or mech) one territory each.” “Mechs can carry workers. Workers carry resources.”
grades.reason: No decisive different-units ruling, resource carriage by all units or carried-worker subsequent movement.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: A unit entering a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat, with a loss of 1 popularity per retreating worker. The summary does not specify whether Speed-enabled movement changes this, whether the rule applies at zero popularity, or whether the mech's workers may enter the territory alone.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Moving into a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat (lose 1 popularity per retreating worker).”
grades.reason: Missing stop, no further turn movement, zero-popularity retreat and independent worker-entry prohibition.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: Combat occurs when your character or mechs share a territory with an opponent's character or mechs after movement. The summary does not specify who chooses the order of multiple combats. It says workers cannot initiate combat and only characters and mechs fight, but does not explain whether workers can enter or leave territory controlled by an enemy character or mech alone.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: “When your character/mechs share a territory with opponent character/mechs after movement.” Special Rules: “Workers cannot initiate combat. Only characters and mechs fight.”
grades.reason: Missing multiple-combat order, before-bottom timing and independent worker enter/leave restriction.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives either 2 Power or 1 Combat Card. Trade costs $1 and gives either 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers or 1 Popularity. The summary does not say what happens if all workers are home or if the combat deck is exhausted.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: “(pay $1): Gain 2 Power on the Power Track, OR draw 1 Combat Card.” Trade: “(pay $1): Gain 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers, OR gain 1 Popularity.”
grades.reason: Missing all-workers-home restriction and exhaustion reshuffle/no-draw branches.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Produce has a variable cost. Choose up to 2 territories you control with workers; each worker on those territories produces 1 resource matching the terrain (Forest Wood, Mountain Metal, Tundra Oil, Farm Food, Village Worker). The summary does not say how the cost is paid, where new workers come from, whether benefits may be declined, or whether new workers change the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce: “(pay variable cost): Choose up to 2 territories you control with workers. Each worker on those territories produces 1 resource matching the terrain.”
grades.reason: Missing exposed costs paid before production, full affordability, optional benefits and left-to-right permanent worker placement/future-cost timing.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs Oil: move a technology cube from a green top-row box to a red bottom-row box to improve action efficiency. Deploy costs Metal: place a mech on a territory with workers and unlock a faction-specific mech ability for your character and all mechs. Placement restrictions beyond “on a territory with workers” and whether a completed bottom action can still be paid are not stated.
grades.reader_evidence: Upgrade: “(pay Oil): Move a technology cube from a green box (top-row) to a red box (bottom-row).” Deploy: “(pay Metal): Place a mech on a territory with workers.”
grades.reason: Missing bracketed/empty box limits, controlled territory/lake restriction and paying completed bottom action.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build costs Wood and places a structure on a territory with workers, with at most one structure per territory. The summary does not say whether structures can move or be destroyed. A Mill counts as an extra territory for Produce; a Mine acts as a personal tunnel adjacent to all other tunnels. How either works when its territory is occupied by enemies is not stated.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: “Place a structure on a territory with workers (max 1 structure per territory).” Structure effects: “Mill: Counts as extra territory for Produce. Mine: Acts as a personal tunnel (adjacent to all other tunnels).”
grades.reason: Missing permanence, legal territories and enemy-controlled Mill/Mine rulings.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Enlist costs Food and places a recruit token, granting one one-time bonus: 2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards. Its ongoing bonus is the specified bonus whenever you or adjacent players take that bottom-row action. The summary does not specify where the token is placed, which action sets its ongoing bonus, or how simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: “Place a recruit token, gaining a one-time bonus (2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards). Ongoing bonus: Gain the specified bonus whenever you OR adjacent players take that bottom-row action.”
grades.reason: Missing open Faction destination/permanence, uncovered-action link and active-left-right/two-player timing.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant secretly selects power from 0 to their current power and may add up to 1 combat card per unit involved; reveal is simultaneous. Highest total wins and the attacker wins ties. The summary does not explain combat abilities or specify further payment/resolution rules for the dial and cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: “Both players secretly select power on their dial (0 to current power). Each player may add up to 1 combat card per unit involved. Reveal simultaneously. Highest total wins (attacker wins ties).”
grades.reason: Dial range incorrectly stated up to current power without cap seven. Missing combat ability priority and payment/discard procedure.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner stays on the territory, keeps resources, and places a combat star. The loser retreats all units to their home base and gains 1 combat card if they committed any power. Popularity changes beyond the separate rule that retreating workers cost 1 popularity per worker are not described.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: “Winner: Stays on territory, keeps resources, places combat star. Loser: Retreats all units to home base, gains 1 combat card if they committed any power.”
grades.reason: Missing attacker versus defender popularity distinction, resource abandonment and explicit card-only retreat-reward branch.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: An encounter is triggered when the character moves onto an encounter token, after all movement and combat. Draw a card with three options and choose one; options can grant resources, popularity, power, etc. The summary does not state what happens if the character loses a contested entry, where encounter gains are placed, or whether normal action costs or bonuses apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Moving character onto an encounter token triggers an encounter after all movement/combat.” Special Rules: “draw a card with three options. Choose one (gain resources, popularity, power, etc.).”
grades.reason: Missing lose/no-encounter branch, benefit destination, affordable printed cost and isolation from mat benefits.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card, which provides a fifth action section on that player's mat. The summary does not say whether later visitors may take one or change cards, or how Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: “The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card providing a 5th action section on their Player mat.”
grades.reason: Missing each character first visit/card permanence and Factory action/movement differences; first-visitor wording insufficient.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: A completed Objective Card is listed as an achievement for placing a star. The summary does not state when it may be revealed, its requirements, what is discarded, or what changes for Saxony.
grades.reader_evidence: Star Placement: “Reveal a completed Objective Card.”
grades.reason: Missing own-turn timing, full requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discard and Saxony second-objective exception.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Listed star achievements are completing all 6 Upgrades, deploying all 4 Mechs, building all 4 Structures, enlisting all 4 Recruits, placing all 8 Workers, revealing a completed Objective Card, winning combat (maximum 2 stars except Saxony unlimited), reaching 18 Popularity, and reaching 16 Power. Whether stars can be lost or another player can block a goal is not stated. The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star.
grades.reader_evidence: Star Placement lists the achievements and Saxony exception. Game End Trigger: “The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star on the Triumph Track.”
grades.reason: Missing irreversible stars and shared non-blocking achievements.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 Popularity the player is in Tier 2 (7–12). The table awards $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per pair of resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory (five territories) add $15. Thirteen resources provide six complete pairs, adding $12, for $47 total from these categories; treatment of an unpaired resource is not specified. Structure bonus tile coins are added, but eligibility is not specified. The stated winner is the player with the most total coins; further victory tiebreakers are not given.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Scoring: “7-12 = Tier 2”; table: “Per Star placed $4,” “Per Territory controlled $3,” “Per 2 Resources controlled $2.” “Plus structure bonus tile coins (varies). Player with the most total coins wins.”
grades.reason: Incorrect Factory value: three territories, not one; result must be $53 rather than $47. Structure eligibility/tiebreakers absent.
